title: Exploring High School EFL Teachers' Experiences with Magic School AI in Lesson Planning: Benefits and Insights
venue: Voices of English Language Education Society
extended_summary:
This paper examines how high school English as a Foreign Language (EFL) teachers perceive and use MagicSchool AI, a generative AI tool, for lesson planning. The central question is whether and how such a tool can support lesson preparation while still preserving pedagogical quality, contextual fit, and teacher judgment.

The study was conducted as an exploratory case study with 38 Indonesian high school EFL teachers in Central Java. Data came from a post-workshop online open-ended questionnaire, focus group interviews, and stimulated recall interviews after teachers had been introduced to AI-assisted lesson planning. The intervention was not a schoolwide coaching system but a workshop-based introduction and subsequent reflection on use of the tool for planning materials, assessments, differentiated texts, and classroom activities.

Findings show that teachers valued MagicSchool AI mainly for speeding up material and assessment preparation, generating diverse instructional ideas, and supporting differentiation for varied learner needs. At the same time, teachers reported that AI outputs often needed substantial refinement, careful prompting, and ongoing human oversight to align with classroom dynamics, vocabulary level, and curriculum goals. The authors conclude that generative AI can be a useful collaborator in lesson planning, but only when paired with teacher expertise, critical evaluation, and professional development in prompt engineering and adaptation.

identified_tools.name: MagicSchool AI
identified_tools.description: A generative AI education tool designed to help teachers create lesson plans, instructional materials, assessments, and other classroom resources through structured prompts and pre-built fields.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a lesson-planning assistant for 38 Indonesian high school EFL teachers after a workshop; teachers used it to generate instructional materials, assessments, differentiated texts, and activity ideas.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that MagicSchool AI reduced the time needed for lesson-material and assessment preparation, especially when using its structured prompts and pre-designed fields. However, some gains were offset by the need for follow-up prompting and refinement, and rural internet connectivity problems reduced practicality for some users.
findings.measure: Teachers’ open-ended questionnaire responses and focus group interviews about time efficiency in material preparation and assessment design

findings.finding_summary: Teachers said the tool supported differentiation by helping them level reading texts, vary complexity, and generate activities aligned with different student needs and learning styles. Respondents emphasized that the outputs were useful starting points but still required human review and adaptation to align with classroom context and curriculum goals.
findings.measure: Teachers’ qualitative reports of differentiation support and adaptability of AI-generated lesson materials

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative exploratory case study based on open-ended questionnaires and focus group interviews, not an experimental or quasi-experimental impact evaluation. The evidence is useful for implementation insights but does not provide causal estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived benefits such as faster planning and easier differentiation, but no effect sizes, standardized outcomes, or student achievement data are reported. The magnitude of impact is therefore unclear and based on teacher self-report.
